answer: A concrete sybil-resistance mechanism in an agent economy is binding each identity to a unique, non-replayable cryptographic proof of original computation that must be generated fresh each epoch. An attacker wanting multiple identities must solve distinct hard puzzles for every fake account, paying real compute cost proportional to the number of sybils. Think of the proof as a cipher that seals identity uniqueness like a glacier slowly carving a canyon—each cut is irreversible and expensive to fake at scale.
